nodes.description: Four missense variants (p.Leu203Phe, recurrent; p.Pro212Leu; p.Gln175Lys; p.Val152Met) and one nonsense variant (p.Cys451Ter) were found in homozygous or compound-heterozygous state. The missense residues lie between the third and fourth armadillo repeats, within the major nuclear localization signal (NLS) binding pocket. All missense mutants were expressed at lower levels than wild-type KPNA7 in transfected cells, the nonsense mutant was undetectable, and the missense mutants bound an SV40 large-T NLS cargo poorly. Because KPNA7 is expressed almost exclusively in oocytes and early embryos, the loss is confined to the maternal contribution to the embryo, which explains the absence of any somatic phenotype.

nodes.description: Model-derived. Kpna2 knockout mouse 1-cell and 2-cell embryos show markedly reduced nascent transcription, and 2-cell embryos down-regulate thousands of genes involved in transcription, RNA metabolism, and translation, including RNA polymerase II-related zygotic genome activation markers. Zygotic genome activation has not been measured in embryos from women with KPNA7 variants, so this node is the proposed human mechanism by analogy.

nodes.description: RSL1D1 (ribosomal L1 domain-containing protein 1), an oocyte-expressed protein with an SV40-like NLS, was identified as a KPNA7 substrate. Patient missense variants reduce KPNA7 binding to RSL1D1 and its nuclear import. In mouse zygotes lacking Kpna2, the functional counterpart of human KPNA7, nuclear RSL1D1 is nearly absent, and oocyte-specific Rsl1d1 knockout reproduces the Kpna2 knockout embryo arrest. RSL1D1 is probably one of several affected cargoes; the others are not identified.

nodes.description: Preclinical only; no treatment for affected women exists. In zygotes from Kpna2 knockout mice, high-dose human KPNA7 cRNA restored RSL1D1 nuclear import and let more than half of the embryos reach the blastocyst stage, whereas mouse Kpna7 cRNA did not. Rescued blastocysts transferred to foster mice did not establish pregnancies. It has not been tried in patient oocytes or embryos.

nodes.description: Kpna2 is the dominant importin alpha in mouse oocytes. Knockout females on an ICR background are otherwise normal but infertile; their oocytes fertilize and cleave once, then arrest at the 2-cell stage with reduced zygotic transcription and poor RSL1D1 nuclear import. Human KPNA7 cRNA, but not mouse Kpna7 cRNA, rescues development to the blastocyst stage.

Females homozygous for either the knockout or the patient-equivalent knock-in were healthy and fertile on C57BL/6 and ICR backgrounds. An earlier independent Kpna7 knockout reported reduced fertility and preferential female fetal loss, so the mouse Kpna7 phenotype ranges from none to subfertility, far milder than the human disease.
